key_facts.fact: VR&E eligibility for Veterans requires a discharge that is not dishonorable and a VA service-connected disability rating of at least 10%.
A VR&E counselor (VRC) determines whether the Veteran has an employment handicap and is eligible, and works with the Veteran on a rehabilitation plan.

Relevant VR&E tracks for finding new work are Rapid Access to Employment (a job search using the Veteran's existing skills) and Employment Through Long-Term Services (education or training for work in a different field).
VR&E services can include help finding and keeping a job, including the use of special employer incentives and job accommodations.
JAN lists telework / work from home as an accommodation for PTSD (under attentiveness/concentration and decreased stamina/fatigue).
For PTSD-related stress, JAN lists accommodations such as a flexible schedule, modified break schedule, counseling, and a support person or support animal.
For leg/mobility impairments, JAN lists accommodations such as adjustable office workstations, periodic rest breaks, a flexible schedule, and telework.

key_facts.fact: VR&E eligibility for Veterans requires a discharge that is not dishonorable and a VA service-connected disability rating of at least 10%.

Compensated Work Therapy (CWT) is a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) clinical vocational rehabilitation program that provides evidence based and evidence informed vocational rehabilitation services. CWT programs are located within all VA medical centers.

IPS is a person-centered approach that is integrated within a treatment team. Also known as supported employment, IPS prioritizes rapid job search for employment opportunities that match with a Veteran’s needs, talents, and preferences and provides ongoing support until steady employment is achieved. IPS Specialist should be aligned under CWT and co-located in office space within proximity to the PTSD and/or MH teams.

The Housing and Urban Development-VA Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH) program is a partnership between the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and VA. Unlike programs that only provide housing assistance, HUD-VASH pairs a housing voucher with ongoing support tailored to each Veteran’s needs. The program is specifically tailored for Veterans experiencing homelessness who have a need for ongoing, intensive case management due to more complex challenges, such as chronic health conditions, that can make finding and maintaining housing more difficult.

Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) grants provide housing stability services to low-income Veteran families who are experiencing homelessness or are at imminent risk of experiencing homelessness through compassionate and responsive services.
VA created Homeless Veteran Community Employment Services (HVCES) to improve employment outcomes for Veterans who have experienced homelessness.

If you are a Veteran who is homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness, we strongly encourage you to contact the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 877-424-3838 for assistance. The call is free, confidential, and available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
